summary: SPHEREx Comet Time Machine is a public web tool that lets anyone see how the sky changes over time in real NASA SPHEREx images. Using data from NASA/IPAC IRSA, it shows interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS across August and December 2025. Visitors drag a time slider, switch infrared wavelengths, and use Blink compare to spot what changed. The tool computes how far the comet moved across the sky between dates and explains each view in plain language, so no astronomy background is needed. Built with Python (data pipeline) and HTML/JavaScript (viewer).
details: SPHEREx Comet Time Machine lets anyone see how the sky changes over time in real SPHEREx images. We used the observation table for interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS from NASA/IPAC IRSA and a Python script (astropy, Pillow) to download small image cut-outs around the comet’s position for 1 and 7 Aug 2025 and 8 and 14 Dec 2025, then converted them to contrast-stretched PNGs. The web viewer (HTML/JavaScript) has a date slider, wavelength selector, Blink compare, crosshair, and a measure of how far the comet moved across the sky. Plain-language explanations make it usable without astronomy knowledge. Limitation: wavelengths differ between dates, and the view is centred on the comet, so background stars drift.Code for the data pipeline and web viewer was written with assistance from Claude (Anthropic). The images are real NASA SPHEREx data, not AI-generated.
